en.p: For an ellipse $C_1$ with foci $\mathrm{F}(0,\,6)$ and $\mathrm{F'}(0,\,-6)$, let $\mathrm{P}$ be the point in the first quadrant where the line through $\mathrm{F}$ parallel to the $x$-axis meets ellipse $C_1$, and let $\mathrm{Q}$ be the point where segment $\mathrm{PF'}$ meets the $x$-axis. For the ellipse $C_2$ with foci $\mathrm{P}$ and $\mathrm{F}$ and a vertex at $\mathrm{Q}$, let $\mathrm{R}$ be the intersection point of the two ellipses $C_1$ and $C_2$ that is closer to the $x$-axis.
When $\overline{\mathrm{F'R}}-\overline{\mathrm{PR}}=7\sqrt{2}$, find the product of the lengths of the major axes of the two ellipses $C_1$ and $C_2$. [4 points]
